hypothesis: P3 attributed 5.7% of warm CPU samples on Lambda to libgomp's spin/barrier code (caller ggml_graph_compute_thread). ggml's barrier is `#pragma omp barrier`, and libgomp's default (OMP_WAIT_POLICY unset) spins 300,000 times before it sleeps on a futex. If that spinning is wasted CPU on a fully used 6-vCPU sandbox (6 OpenMP threads on 6 vCPUs, plus Python's own threads), shortening or removing it makes warm requests up to ~5% faster. Passive waiting may instead add futex wake-up latency at every barrier and slow them. Thread count (6) is not varied.

conclusion: GOMP_SPINCOUNT=30000 (one tenth of libgomp's default spin before the futex sleep) makes warm requests faster. Warm REPORT Duration paired by (round, request) on CPU part 0xd40: -5.40% mean over 9 rounds (every round below 0, range -6.93 to -4.85%; 45 cells; exact sign-flip p=0.00391; control split-half noise at most 3.05%). Median warm REPORT Duration 605 -> 577 ms; engine timer -5.39%. Mechanism (measured): process CPU per warm request -1.05%, voluntary context switches 370 -> 3821 per request. Other CPU parts, same direction, too few rounds to test: 0xd0c: -7.7% over 3 round(s) (3 below 0, 0 above), underpowered; 0xd4f: -4.8% over 4 round(s) (4 below 0, 0 above), underpowered. Against passive in the same rounds on 0xd40 the difference is -0.24 percentage points mean per round, 6 of 9 rounds below 0, sign-flip p=0.32422: the two are not distinguishable, so the gain comes from not spinning for the default 300,000 iterations, not from a particular short count. Side effects: cold first request -0.081 s, 95% CI [-0.190, +0.001] (n=[52, 50]); restored first request +0.003 s [-0.070, +0.107] (n=[29, 29]), its inference -17 ms [-31, -2]; cold max memory +0 MB. Recommendation: adopt with passive as equivalent; prefer passive for the simpler setting, or this one if a later rung shows passive wake-up cost. Correctness: 1440/1440 answers bit-identical to ctl for the same request and CPU part in this run, and 5579/5579 bit-identical to P1's reference where it covers the CPU part. libgomp's own start-up print (OMP_DISPLAY_ENV=VERBOSE) shows GOMP_SPINCOUNT=30000 on this arm and 300000 on ctl, so the variable reached the library. Errors in the whole run: 0 function errors and 1 client-side transport error (passive warm, restore leg round 2: SSL EOF after 0.4 s, no REPORT line in the saved logs, so Lambda never ran it); it is published, and carries no answer or latency. Restore rows with client:ReadTimeoutError: 0. Host: CPU parts 0xd40, 0xd0c and 0xd4f as read from /proc/cpuinfo, every comparison is within one part, and no CPU generation is inferred. Warm arms are interleaved pass by pass within each round; cold and restore are sequential arm waves whose order rotates across rounds. Run cost $3.98 (all four arms).

unknown.cgroup: per environment in e13.host.identities; any file the sandbox hides is 'unknown'

host_variability.method: Every comparison is made within one observed CPU part. Warm (the primary metric): within each round the arms alternate pass by pass (the arm order rotates every pass), so the arms are interleaved within the round, and each (round, request) cell is compared on the same CPU part. Cold and restore waves are sequential arm waves whose position rotates across rounds (a Latin square over 4 rounds): that controls order and round drift but not time-within-round drift. Rows without a CPU part are counted, never compared.
